::: {.bnr-manual-flag .bnr-manual-flag--operations}
Operations Manual
:::

## Purpose

Use this workflow for every authorised CVD mortality release. The six steps take the data from the mortality REDCap project, classify CVD deaths, calculate the statistics, support human review and approval, and publish the approved files.

This is separate from the CVD event preparation workflow. Steps 1–5 create private working files. Only Step 6 moves approved files into the public area.

## Before starting

- First use [Authorise a data export](../release/data-release.qmd) to confirm the reporting period and authority to proceed.
- Work on the authorised workstation with the private workspace available.
- Confirm the configured mortality REDCap access is available.
- Confirm **User > BNR > Update CVD mortality dashboard** is present in Stata.
- Use the same release year (`YYYY`) and month (`MM`) throughout.
- Leave replacement options off unless a rerun has been deliberately authorised.

## Step 1: extract the mortality data

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Details"}
| Question | Details |
|---|---|
| What this step does | Extracts the death-certificate records from the mortality REDCap project and prepares the private all-deaths source data through the authorised month-end. Records with a valid death date after the cut-off are excluded; records with a missing or invalid death date remain visible for checking. This step does not classify Heart, Stroke or underlying cause of death. The resulting data contain personally identifiable information and must remain private.|
| How to run it | In Stata, choose **User > BNR > Update CVD mortality dashboard > Step 1: Extract REDCap data**. Enter the authorised year and month, then run the extract. |
| What to check | Confirm that the summary says the step completed successfully. Check that the release cut-off, number of retained records and death-date range are plausible. Investigate any missing or invalid death dates before relying on the affected records. |
| Files and location | Step 1 creates `bnr_mort_s1_YYYYMM_raw.csv`, `bnr_mort_s1_YYYYMM.dta` and `bnr_mort_s1_YYYYMM_manifest.yml` in `$BNR_DATA_RAW/redcap/mortality/yYYYY/mMM/`. The CSV and Stata dataset contain confidential information and must remain private. The Step 1 log is under `$BNR_PRIVATE_LOGS/`. |
| Technical detail | See [Mortality Step 1: Extract mortality data](../../technical/workflows/mortality/extract.qmd) for the approved source fields, dialog settings, exact checks and troubleshooting. |
:::

## Step 2: classify CVD deaths

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Details"}
| Question | Details |
|---|---|
| What this step does | Applies the fixed BNR classifier to the death-certificate wording and structure. It identifies evidence for All CVD, Heart and Stroke and assigns the Clear, Likely and Possible classes used in Primary and Inclusive reporting. This is an approximate BNR classification, not formal national underlying-cause coding. Direct identity fields are removed, but the data still contain internal identifiers and death-certificate text and must remain private.|
| How to run it | In the mortality menu, choose **Step 2: Classify causes of death**. Enter the same release year and month used in Step 1, then run the step. |
| What to check | Confirm that the summary says the step completed successfully. Review the class counts and open the classification review and source-structure summary files. Investigate unexpected changes, uncertain source structures and any warnings before continuing. |
| Files and location | Step 2 reads `$BNR_DATA_RAW/redcap/mortality/yYYYY/mMM/bnr_mort_s1_YYYYMM.dta`. It creates `bnr_mort_s2_YYYYMM.dta`, a classification summary, a targeted review file, a source-structure summary and a YAML receipt in `$BNR_DATA_DERIVED/mortality/yYYYY/mMM/`. The Step 2 log is under `$BNR_PRIVATE_LOGS/`. All outputs remain private. |
| Technical detail | See [Mortality Step 2: Classify CVD deaths](../../technical/workflows/mortality/classify.qmd) for the evidence classes, reporting definitions, exact file names and change-control rules. |
:::

## Step 3: calculate the mortality statistics

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Details"}
| Question | Details |
|---|---|
| What this step does | Uses the classified deaths to calculate results for the Primary and Inclusive mortality definitions. These include annual, quarterly and monthly counts; annual percentage distributions; annual and quarterly previous-five-year comparisons; and annual crude and age-standardised rates. It creates a private staging package containing exact, unsuppressed aggregate values. It does not apply the final public disclosure controls, approve or publish the release. The package remains confidential and private.|
| How to run it | In the mortality menu, choose **Step 3: Build mortality burden data**. Enter the same release year and month used in Steps 1 and 2, then run the step. |
| What to check | Confirm that the summary says the step completed successfully. Check that the analysis begins in 2010 and ends with the expected latest complete calendar year. Review the row counts for the Primary and Inclusive definitions, the automated QA file and the suppression worklist. Confirm that the `datasets/`, `metadata/` and `review/` folders and `readme.txt` are present. The suppression workbook is an automated worklist; Step 4 creates the human-review package. |
| Files and location | Step 3 reads `$BNR_DATA_DERIVED/mortality/yYYYY/mMM/bnr_mort_s2_YYYYMM.dta`. Rate calculations also use the approved population files under `$BNR_PRIVATE/data/reference/population/`. The staging package is created in `$BNR_STAGING/mortality/burden/mort_YYYY_MM/`, and the Step 3 log is under `$BNR_PRIVATE_LOGS/`. |
| Technical detail | See [Mortality Step 3: Build mortality burden data](../../technical/workflows/mortality/build-burden.qmd) for the reporting structure, exact files, population sources and automated checks. |
:::

## Step 4: review the mortality release

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Details"}
| Question | Details |
|---|---|
| What this step does | Rechecks the Step 3 package, applies the approved disclosure-control rules and creates the aggregated dataset for public release. It also creates the fixed 2015–2019 monthly reference and the files needed for human review. It does not calculate new rates, approve or publish the release. |
| How to run it | In the mortality menu, choose **Step 4: Review mortality release**. Enter the same release year and month, then run the step. Open the review workbook identified by **OPEN THIS FILE FIRST** in the summary. |
| What to check | Confirm the release identity and analysis period. Review the results for the Primary and Inclusive definitions, crude and age-standardised rates, automated QA, protected rows and proposed public candidate. Check that protected values and their related values have been hidden correctly. Confirm that the monthly reference contains 24 rows: one row for each month for both reporting definitions, based on 2015–2019 All-CVD deaths for both sexes and all ages. Decide whether the release is plausible, safe and ready for approval. |
| Files and location | Step 4 writes `mort_s4_candidate.dta`, `mort_s4_review_mort_YYYY_MM.xlsx`, the QA receipt, the review-basis file and the three monthly-reference files to `$BNR_STAGING/mortality/burden/mort_YYYY_MM/review/`. The Step 4 log is under `$BNR_PRIVATE_LOGS/`. All these files remain private. |
| Technical detail | See [Mortality Step 4: Review the mortality release](../../technical/workflows/mortality/review.qmd) for the workbook sheets, full review list, disclosure-control rules and exact files. |
:::

## Step 5: approve the reviewed release

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Details"}
| Question | Details |
|---|---|
| What this step does | Records an authorised person's approval of the exact candidate reviewed in Step 4. It checks that the reviewed files have not changed, creates the private public-ready package and writes the approval record last. It does not publish the files. |
| How to run it | Complete the Step 4 review first. In the mortality menu, choose **Step 5: Approve reviewed mortality release**. Enter the release year and month, the approver's full name and one of the authorised roles: BNR Lead or BNR Analyst. Complete all five confirmations, then record the approval. |
| What to check | Confirm that the summary reports **APPROVED - PENDING STEP 6**. Open `approval.yml` and check the release, package, approver, role, disclosure status and manifest details. Confirm that `public_manifest.csv` lists exactly ten payload files. Approval is complete only when all five review confirmations have been made and the approval file exists. |
| Files and location | Step 5 creates `$BNR_STAGING/mortality/burden/mort_YYYY_MM/public_ready/`. Its `datasets/` and `metadata/` folders contain the ten approved data and metadata files. The private controls `public_manifest.csv` and `approval.yml` are in the root of `public_ready/`. The Step 5 log is under `$BNR_PRIVATE_LOGS/`. |
| Technical detail | See [Mortality Step 5: Approve the reviewed release](../../technical/workflows/mortality/approve.qmd) for the authorised roles, five confirmations, exact ten-file payload and approval controls. |
:::

## Step 6: publish the approved files

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Details"}
| Question | Details |
|---|---|
| What this step does | Checks the approval, manifest and all ten approved files before copying them across the private-to-public boundary. It creates the release ZIP and catalogue record in the authoritative public area, then refreshes the website-download copy from that public area. It does not recalculate, apply disclosure control or approve the statistics. |
| How to run it | In the mortality menu, choose **Step 6: Publish approved mortality outputs**. Enter the approved release year and month, then run Step 6. Leave the replacement option off for a first publication. |
| What to check | Confirm that the summary reports **Run status: PUBLISHED** and **Verification: PASSED**. Inspect the authoritative public package and website copy. Open the release ZIP and confirm that it contains the ten approved files. Check the catalogue record and confirm that `approval.yml`, `public_manifest.csv` and private review files were not published. |
| Files and location | The authoritative public package is under `$BNR_PUBLIC/metrics/mortality/burden/`. The website copy is under `$BNR_REPO/site/downloads/files/metrics/mortality/burden/`. The stable dashboard dataset is `datasets/mort_burden_metrics_current.csv`, and the fixed monthly reference is `datasets/mort_monthly_reference_2015_2019.csv`. The Step 6 log is under `$BNR_PRIVATE_LOGS/`. |
| Technical detail | Step 6 does not rebuild the central Downloads catalogue or render the website. After it completes, rebuild the catalogue through the normal site-render process and inspect the mortality dashboard and Downloads page before committing and deploying the website. See [Mortality Step 6: Publish approved mortality outputs](../../technical/workflows/mortality/publish.qmd) for the full verification checks and public package structure. |
:::

## If a step needs attention

This workflow is automated and is designed to stop when an expected input, data structure or check does not match. Routine releases should normally complete reliably while the REDCap fields, data structures, configured paths and reference files remain unchanged. Problems should therefore be uncommon, and a stopped run is a protection rather than evidence that the whole system has failed.

Do not move to the next step until the issue is understood and resolved. Do not repair generated outputs by editing or copying individual files by hand.

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| A step fails or does not finish | Read its summary and private log. Check the reported input, access, setting, file location or data issue. If the cause is clear, correct the earliest affected source or setting and rerun from that step. |
| A required input, receipt or output is missing | Check that the preceding step completed for the same release year and month. Do not create or copy a replacement file by hand. |
| The Step 2 classifications or source-structure results are surprising | Compare the classification summary, review file and structure summary with the previous successful release. Discuss unexplained changes with the BNR Lead or Analyst before continuing. |
| The Step 3 analysis years, counts, distributions or rates are surprising | Check the selected release, classified input and population reference files. Do not continue to disclosure review until the results are understood. |
| A new month fails but the previous month succeeded | First compare the new month's run summary, input structure and record patterns with the previous successful release. This can help distinguish a current-data problem from a wider access, configuration or code problem. A previous month may be rerun only as a controlled test in a separate test copy or with deliberate replacement authorisation; do not replace live outputs merely to diagnose a failure. |
| A disclosure-control check fails or a protected value remains visible | Do not approve or publish. Correct the earliest affected source, reference, configuration or version-controlled code, rerun from there and complete Step 4 review again. |
| Step 4 is rebuilt or a reviewed file changes | Complete the human review again before approval. Step 5 must approve the exact unchanged candidate and reference files produced by the latest Step 4 run. |
| Step 6 stops after publication has begun | Inspect both `$BNR_PUBLIC/metrics/mortality/burden/` and the website-download copy before rerunning. Use the replacement option only after confirming what was already copied. |
| Private content appears in Git status or a public folder | Stop publication immediately. Remove the private content through the approved recovery process and seek support before continuing. |
